title: M1 First publish - wirekit 0.1.0 core, four providers, and release preparation

overview.problemStatement: The workspace holds one crate, dado. wirekit does not exist, and neither do the four providers named for the first publish. Without a shared core, each provider would grow its own error enum, retry loop, rate limiter, and auth handling, which is the fragmentation wirekit exists to remove and a direct violation of CON-207. Without a release-ready package, external developers cannot install anything. The backlog records this as M1 (BP-005 to BP-010) and marks BP-005 the shared model for all of M1, M2, and M3.
overview.proposedSolution: Deliver M1 as one feature on one branch, mirroring how m0-foundation covered BP-001 to BP-004. First, a wirekit core: one #[non_exhaustive] WirekitError with stable W#### codes; one retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter, 3 attempts by default, retry on 5xx/429/network, honor Retry-After, never retry other 4xx); a hand-rolled per-provider token bucket; one shared reqwest::Client with HTTPS-only base URLs; an auth layer (Bearer, Basic, API key header/query, HMAC, OAuth2 client credentials) over a redacting Secret<T>; tracing for start, finish, retry, rate-limit hit, and error; and one pipeline (auth, rate limit, retry, send, decode) with the CON-213 body-level error hook. Second, four feature-gated provider modules: NOAA (no auth, forecasts and alerts), Twilio (Basic or API key, form-encoded, SMS/WhatsApp/voice/MFA/lookup, X-Twilio-Signature), SendGrid (Bearer, JSON, templates, sandbox, errors[], ECDSA event webhook), and Slack (bot token, ok:false at HTTP 200, X-Slack-Signature). Third, release preparation: changelog, complete metadata, provider matrix, feature-flag table, error reference, one runnable example per provider, a verified cargo publish -p wirekit --dry-run, and a wirekit section in RELEASING.md. The real cargo publish and the wirekit-v0.1.0 tag stay manual post-merge, like dado.
overview.targetAudience: External Rust developers installing wirekit 0.1.0 who expect one error type, one retry policy, and one auth layer across providers, plus the M2/M3 crates (platform-core, quota-ledger, hookgate) that consume this contract and the first production consumers (GIA, OmniStream).
assumptions: The crate name wirekit is available on crates.io; it MUST be re-checked immediately before publication (CON-111). Availability is not verified by this feature.
The chosen dependency versions are MSRV 1.85 compatible and stay so; an MSRV CI job guards this (CON-102).
rustls is the preferred TLS backend; native-tls is a documented alternative, not the default.
Provider integrations remain feature-gated modules of wirekit, never separate crates (CON-104).
The core is always compiled; default = [] means no provider module enabled, not no core.
dado is a sequencing dependency only; wirekit does not call dado.
Every provider has a design file following the 03-28 pattern, satisfying CON-105 before implementation.
Provider credentials come from the caller; no live provider account is used to build or verify this feature.
Test authoring belongs to /sdrive:test, not this feature's implementation tasks.
The four providers are validated against recorded or sandbox fixtures, never against production traffic.
outOfScope: Providers beyond NOAA, Twilio, SendGrid, and Slack (the remaining catalogue/ providers, including Stripe, Meta, EagleView, QuickBooks, and the Google OAuth helper)
OAuth2 Authorization Code + PKCE, browser redirects, and multi-tenant install flows (Slack install and Google OAuth belong to BP-015 per CON-212)
Stateful concerns: shared quota accounting (quota-ledger), webhook delivery state, dedupe stores, and outboxes (hookgate), and the tenant/provider registry (platform-core)
MFA orchestration policy, messaging compliance decisions, and message templating owned by the consuming application
Streaming uploads/downloads, WebSocket or gateway transports (Slack Socket Mode, Twilio Media Streams), and multipart file transfer beyond a single-body request
Application domain types, billing rules, and product workflows (CON-106)
Publishing wirekit from the feature branch and creating the wirekit-v0.1.0 tag; both are manual post-merge steps

userStories.title: Handle every provider failure with one error type
userStories.want: one WirekitError type that every provider maps into
userStories.benefit: I write one error handler instead of one per provider

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a provider response with a non-2xx status, when the pipeline maps the failure, then it returns WirekitError::Api { status, code, message } and no provider-specific error type appears in the public API.
Given any WirekitError, when code() is called, then it returns a stable &'static str of the form W####, and Display renders the code with a message.
Given any WirekitError, when Debug and Display are printed, then no credential, token, or raw request/response body appears.
Given the WirekitError enum, when a consumer matches it with a wildcard arm, then the match compiles, proving #[non_exhaustive].
Given WirekitError, when used with ? or as Box<dyn std::error::Error>, then it implements std::error::Error and exposes source() for wrapped causes.

userStories.title: Get the same retry behavior from every provider
userStories.want: one retry policy that applies everywhere
userStories.benefit: I am not debugging why one provider retries and another does not

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a 5xx response and the default policy, when the request is executed, then it is retried up to 3 attempts total, and the final failure is WirekitError::Api carrying the last status.
Given a 429 response with a Retry-After header, when the request is retried, then the delay is at least the header value, and an exhausted policy yields WirekitError::RateLimit { retry_after }.
Given a 400, 401, 403, or 404 response, when executed, then no retry occurs and the error returns immediately.
Given a network or timeout failure, when executed, then it is retried and ends as WirekitError::Network or WirekitError::Timeout.
Given the retry policy, when delays are computed, then they grow exponentially with bounded jitter and stay within the configured bounds.
Given a retry, when it occurs, then a tracing event records the attempt number and the delay.

userStories.title: Respect per-provider rate limits
userStories.want: rate limiting handled in one place
userStories.benefit: I do not build rate limiting per API

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a configured per-provider token bucket, when requests exceed the configured rate, then the limiter throttles them so the rate is not exceeded.
Given two providers with different rate configurations, when both send requests, then each uses its own bucket and its own override.
Given a rate-limit hit, when it occurs, then a tracing metric event is emitted.
Given an empty bucket, when a request waits for a token, then the async task yields instead of blocking the runtime thread (no std::thread::sleep).

userStories.title: Share one HTTP client pool
userStories.benefit: connections are reused and memory is bounded

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given no injected client, when two providers send requests, then they share one reqwest::Client and therefore one connection pool.
Given a caller-injected reqwest::Client, when a request is sent, then the injected client is used verbatim and no second pool is created.
Given the client builder, when timeouts, TLS, a proxy, and default headers are configured, then those settings apply to requests.
Given an http:// base URL, when a request is prepared, then it is rejected with WirekitError::InvalidConfig before any socket is opened.
Given the default configuration, when the client is built, then a request timeout and connection-pool limits are applied.

userStories.title: Apply authentication consistently
userStories.benefit: every provider using the same scheme reuses it

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a bearer token, when a request is sent, then Authorization: Bearer <token> is applied.
Given basic credentials, when a request is sent, then Authorization: Basic <base64(user:pass)> is applied.
Given an API key configured for a header, when a request is sent, then the configured header carries the key.
Given an API key configured for the query string, when a request is sent, then the key is added as a query parameter.
Given the HMAC scheme, when a request is signed, then the signature is computed over the canonical raw request bytes and compared with a constant-time routine.
Given OAuth2 client credentials, when a request is made without a valid token, then a token is fetched, cached, and reused, and is refreshed before expiry.
Given an auth or secret type, when Debug/Display are printed, then the secret renders as ***, and no secret field implements Serialize.

userStories.title: Observe every call
userStories.benefit: I can plug in OpenTelemetry, Datadog, or Jaeger once

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a request, when it starts, then a tracing event with the method and the redacted URL is emitted.
Given a completed request, when it finishes, then a tracing event records the duration.
Given a retry, a rate-limit hit, or an error, when it occurs, then the matching tracing event is emitted.
Given any of these events, when they are recorded, then no credential or token appears in the output.

userStories.title: Implement a provider against one pipeline
userStories.want: to declare a URL, method, body, and response type
userStories.benefit: I do not reimplement auth, retry, rate limiting, tracing, or error mapping

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a provider that declares a URL, method, body, and response type, when it executes, then the pipeline applies auth, rate limit, retry, send, and decode in that order.
Given a successful response, when decoded, then the caller's typed value is returned via serde.
Given HTTP 200 with a body-level error (Slack ok: false or a GraphQL errors[] array), when the body hook is configured, then WirekitError::Api is returned instead of a success (CON-213).
Given a malformed body, when decoding fails, then WirekitError::Decode is returned and no panic occurs.
Given missing credentials, when a request is prepared, then WirekitError::InvalidConfig is returned and no request is sent.

userStories.title: Keep the crate safe, dependency-honest, and lint-clean
userStories.want: the crate to stay within its stated job
userStories.benefit: it can be a dependency of any Rust application

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the crate root, when compiled, then #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and #![deny(missing_docs)] are present and every public item is documented.
Given the crate, when built with default features and with each provider feature independently, then it compiles, and features are additive (CON-204).
Given Rust 1.85, when the workspace builds, then wirekit compiles under edition 2021.
Given the crate, when inspected, then it introduces no database, tenant, billing, or application-domain types (CON-106, CON-107).
Given the crate's source, when scanned, then it does not read .env files or environment files to obtain credentials (CON-519).
Given the full test suite, when it runs, then every acceptance criterion has at least one test, supplied by the Test agent (CON-404).

userStories.title: Fetch forecasts and alerts from NOAA with no API key
userStories.benefit: I can build a weather pipeline without managing credentials

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a latitude and longitude or a grid point, when a point forecast is requested, then a typed response with periods, temperature, and precipitation is returned.
Given an area or zone, when active alerts are listed, then typed alert values with alert ID, event, severity, areas, and description are returned.
Given an alert ID, when it is fetched, then the single alert is returned; an unknown ID returns WirekitError::Api carrying the reported status.
Given a problem+json body (type, title, status, detail), when the response reports a failure, then it maps to WirekitError::Api with the reported status and detail.
Given a request built without the required descriptive User-Agent, when it is sent, then it is rejected with WirekitError::InvalidConfig (NOAA asks for an identifying agent).
Given caching enabled, when the same grid or zone is requested again within the TTL, then the cached value is reused instead of a new call.
Given a 429 or 5xx from NOAA, when the request is retried, then the shared backoff policy applies and Retry-After is honored.

userStories.title: Send SMS, WhatsApp, voice, MFA, and lookup through Twilio
userStories.benefit: SMS, voice, MFA, and number lookup share the same auth, retry, and error model

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given account credentials, when the client is built, then Basic auth (Account SID and Auth Token) or API-key-plus-secret is applied to every request.
Given a send-SMS request, when it is sent, then the body is form-encoded to the messages endpoint and a typed response carrying the message SID is returned.
Given a send-WhatsApp request, when it is sent, then it is delivered through the WhatsApp sender and a typed response is returned.
Given a call request with TwiML, when it is sent, then a call is created and a typed status is returned; fetching status returns the current value.
Given an MFA challenge, when it is started and then verified, then typed challenge and verification results are returned.
Given a phone number, when it is looked up, then a typed lookup result with validation data is returned.
Given Twilio's code, message, and HTTP status, when a failure occurs, then WirekitError::Api { status, code, message } is returned, and an authentication failure maps to WirekitError::Auth.

Given a webhook body and X-Twilio-Signature, when it is verified, then the signature is computed over the request URL plus the sorted form parameters with HMAC-SHA1 and compared in constant time; a tampered body fails verification.
Given a per-account token bucket, when the configured rate is exceeded, then sends are throttled and the remaining quota is surfaced through tracing.

userStories.title: Send transactional email through SendGrid
userStories.want: typed email and template support with correct failure handling
userStories.benefit: delivery failures are visible and templates are reusable

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an API key, when the client is built, then bearer authentication is applied and the key is never logged.
Given a send-email request, when it is sent, then a typed result carrying the X-Message-Id is returned.
Given a template request with substitutions, when it is sent, then the dynamic template is rendered server-side and the message is delivered.
Given sandbox mode enabled, when a send is requested, then the request is validated without delivering mail.
Given an errors[] array in the body, when the request fails, then WirekitError::Api carries the first code and message and the full list is retained in details.
Given an event-webhook body and signature, when it is verified with the configured public key, then a valid signature passes, and a re-serialized body fails verification (CON-215).
Given repeated events carrying the same sg_event_id, when they are received, then duplicates are identifiable so the caller can dedupe.
Given an attachment, when it is sent, then base64 and URL attachments are supported within the documented size and MIME limits.

userStories.title: Post notifications to Slack and handle body-level errors

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a bot token, when the client is built, then the token is applied to requests and never appears in logs or traces.
Given a text message or a Block Kit payload, when it is posted, then a typed result carrying the channel and timestamp is returned.
Given an HTTP 200 response with ok: false, when the body reports an error, then WirekitError::Api carries the error string and the call is not treated as a success (CON-213).
Given channel_not_found or not_in_channel, when the request fails, then no retry occurs.
Given a 429 with Retry-After, when the request is retried, then the header is honored and cached channel data reduces repeated lookups.
Given a request body with X-Slack-Signature and X-Slack-Request-Timestamp, when it is verified, then the HMAC-SHA256 signature is validated over the raw bytes and a stale timestamp is rejected.
Given a file, when it is uploaded, then it is uploaded within the documented size and type limits.
Given a channel or user query, when it is requested, then typed channel and user results are returned.

userStories.title: Publish wirekit 0.1.0 reproducibly
userStories.want: a release-ready package and a documented runbook
userStories.benefit: the first publish is safe, verifiable, and repeatable

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given cargo package -p wirekit --list, when it runs, then the package includes Cargo.toml, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, src/**, examples/**, and the license files.
Given a clean tree, when cargo publish -p wirekit --dry-run runs, then it succeeds.
Given the published package metadata, when inspected, then repository, readme, keywords, categories, license, rust-version, and the docs.rs all-features setting resolve correctly.
Given crates/wirekit/CHANGELOG.md, when read, then a 0.1.0 entry describes the core and the four providers.
Given the repository documentation, when read, then a provider matrix lists the four providers with their auth scheme, base URL, and feature flag.
Given the crate documentation, when read, then a feature-flag table and an error reference (the W#### codes) are present.

Given the examples directory, when cargo build --examples --all-features runs, then one example per provider compiles; examples needing credentials exit with a clear message when they are absent, and the NOAA example runs without a key.
Given RELEASING.md, when followed for wirekit, then it covers pre-flight, version and changelog, dry-run, the wirekit-v0.1.0 tag, publish, verification, and yank or rollback.

functionalRequirements.text: The repository MUST contain a wirekit crate as a workspace member at crates/wirekit, version 0.1.0, inheriting edition, rust-version, and license from [workspace.package].
The crate MUST compile with default = [], always expose the core, and gate every provider module behind a separate additive feature.
The crate MUST declare #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and #![deny(missing_docs)], and every public item MUST have a rustdoc comment.
A single #[non_exhaustive] WirekitError enum MUST be the only error type on the public API.
Every WirekitError variant MUST expose a stable code() string of the form W#### and MUST implement Display and std::error::Error.
Provider failures MUST map into WirekitError::Api { status, code, message }; a provider MUST NOT introduce a second error type.
WirekitError's Debug, Display, logs, traces, and payloads MUST NOT contain credentials, tokens, or raw bodies.
HTTP retries MUST use exponential backoff with jitter and 3 attempts by default.
Retries MUST occur on 5xx, 429, and network or timeout errors, and MUST honor Retry-After.
Retries MUST NOT occur on any other 4xx status.
The retry policy MUST be configurable per client for attempt count, base delay, maximum delay, and jitter bounds.
Rate limiting MUST be a per-provider token bucket with per-provider overrides.
The rate limiter MUST emit a tracing event for every rate-limit hit.
The crate MUST share one pooled reqwest::Client per process unless the caller injects its own client.
The client builder MUST allow configuring timeouts, TLS, proxying, and default headers.
The client MUST reject non-HTTPS base URLs with WirekitError::InvalidConfig.
The auth layer MUST provide Bearer, Basic, API-key-in-header, API-key-in-query, HMAC-signature, and OAuth2-client-credentials schemes.
OAuth2 client credentials MUST fetch a token, cache it, and refresh it before expiry, with a single in-flight fetch per client.
Auth and secret types MUST redact secrets in Debug/Display and MUST NOT implement Serialize for a secret field.
Every outbound request MUST emit tracing events for start, finish with duration, retry, rate-limit hit, and error.
The core MUST expose one request pipeline (auth, rate limit, retry, send, decode) so a provider supplies only a URL, method, body, and response type.
The core MUST expose a body-level error hook so that HTTP 200 with a body-reported error maps to WirekitError::Api.
Response bodies MUST decode into caller types via serde, and a decode failure MUST return WirekitError::Decode rather than a panic.
The crate MUST treat URLs, header values, and response bytes as untrusted and MUST NOT panic on malformed input.
Credentials MUST come from caller-supplied configuration or secret stores; the crate MUST NOT read .env or environment files.
The crate MUST be publishable as wirekit 0.1.0 with complete metadata and a docs.rs all-features configuration.
The crate MUST expose a noaa feature-gated module with typed forecast, alert, and radar metadata models.
NOAA requests MUST carry a descriptive User-Agent, and a request without one MUST be rejected with WirekitError::InvalidConfig.
NOAA problem+json failures MUST map to WirekitError::Api with the reported status and detail.
The NOAA module SHOULD cache forecasts and alerts by grid or zone with a configurable TTL.
The crate MUST expose a twilio feature-gated module with typed SMS, WhatsApp, voice, MFA, and lookup models.
Twilio requests MUST be form-encoded and authenticate with Basic (Account SID plus Auth Token) or an API key and secret.
Twilio failures MUST map code, message, and HTTP status into WirekitError::Api, and authentication failures into WirekitError::Auth.
The Twilio module MUST verify X-Twilio-Signature over the raw request bytes with constant-time comparison.
The Twilio module MUST apply a per-account token bucket and surface remaining quota through tracing.
The crate MUST expose a sendgrid feature-gated module with typed email, template, attachment, and contact-list models.
SendGrid MUST authenticate with a bearer API key and MUST support a sandbox mode that validates without delivering.
SendGrid errors MUST map its errors[] array into WirekitError::Api with the first code and message, retaining the full list in details.
The SendGrid module MUST verify the event-webhook signature on the raw body bytes against a configured public key.
The crate MUST expose a slack feature-gated module with typed messages, Block Kit blocks, channels, users, and file uploads.
The Slack module MUST treat HTTP 200 with ok: false as an error mapped to WirekitError::Api, and MUST NOT treat 200 as success.
The Slack module MUST verify X-Slack-Signature over the raw bytes and MUST reject a stale X-Slack-Request-Timestamp.
Slack channel_not_found and not_in_channel MUST NOT be retried.
Provider modules MUST NOT introduce a second error type; every failure maps into WirekitError.
The crate MUST include one runnable example per provider, a provider matrix, a feature-flag table, and an error reference.
The crate MUST include a 0.1.0 changelog entry and complete publishable metadata with docs.rs all-features.
cargo publish -p wirekit --dry-run MUST succeed from a clean tree.
RELEASING.md MUST document the wirekit release with the tag wirekit-v0.1.0.
Each provider module MUST be gated by its own additive feature that MUST NOT enable or be enabled by another provider feature.
Every provider MUST use the shared core pipeline for auth, retry, rate limiting, tracing, and error mapping.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: The crate MUST compile on Rust 1.85 with edition 2021.
The crate MUST keep forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs); docs MUST build with warnings denied.
Features MUST be additive; enabling a provider feature MUST NOT enable or disable another feature, and the default feature set MUST be documented.
The crate MUST NOT force a database, tenant model, quota state, webhook state, or application-domain types on consumers.
Retry backoff and token-bucket waiting MUST yield to the async runtime and MUST NOT block a runtime thread.
The shared client MUST bound resource usage through default timeouts and connection-pool limits.
Secrets MUST be redacted in Debug, Display, logs, traces, and error payloads, and MUST NOT be serialized.
The crate MUST treat all network input as untrusted and MUST NOT panic, abort, or hang on malformed responses.
Every acceptance criterion MUST be covered by at least one test, supplied by the Test agent.
The crate MUST NOT expose a global mutable singleton; client and provider construction MUST be explicit.

Authentication (CON-511) - the pipeline MUST apply the configured auth scheme to every outbound request for every provider and MUST fail closed with WirekitError::InvalidConfig when credentials are missing.
Rate limiting (CON-514) - the per-provider token bucket MUST be enforced before every outbound request, with per-provider overrides.
Input validation (CON-515) - URLs, header values, form bodies, and response bodies MUST be validated; malformed input MUST return a typed WirekitError and MUST NOT panic.
Environment security (CON-519) - credentials MUST come from caller-supplied configuration or secret stores; the crate MUST NOT read .env files and MUST NOT commit secrets.
HTTPS (CON-520) - all outbound requests MUST use TLS; non-HTTPS base URLs MUST be rejected before any socket is opened.
Webhook signature verification MUST operate on the raw request bytes; a body MUST NOT be re-serialized before verification (CON-215).
Provider secrets (auth tokens, API keys, signing secrets, webhook public keys where sensitive) MUST be redacted in Debug, Display, logs, and traces.
Each provider module MUST use the shared retry policy and MUST NOT implement its own retry loop.
A provider MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 as success when the body reports an error (CON-213).
The four provider features MUST be additive, independently compilable, and MSRV 1.85 compatible.
Provider modules MUST NOT contain application domain types, billing rules, or vendor workflow code (CON-106).
Published documentation, examples, and fixtures MUST NOT contain committed credentials or real provider tokens.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Wait at least the header value, then retry; if attempts are exhausted, return WirekitError::RateLimit { retry_after }.
Apply jittered exponential backoff.
WirekitError::Api carrying the last status and any parsed code and message.
No retry; WirekitError::Api returned immediately.
Retried, then WirekitError::Network.
Retried, then WirekitError::Timeout.

edgeCases.description: Retry-After given as an HTTP date, or unparseable
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Parsed safely; an unparseable value falls back to backoff without panicking.
The request waits asynchronously and proceeds when a token is available.
WirekitError::Auth; no retry on a non-429 4xx.
Refreshed before the next request, never during a partially sent one.

edgeCases.description: HTTP 200 with Slack ok: false or a GraphQL errors[] array
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: WirekitError::Api via the body-level error hook (CON-213).
WirekitError::Decode; no panic.
Rejected before any socket is opened.
Used verbatim; no second pool and no overridden configuration.
Share one bucket so the aggregate rate is respected.
Debug prints ***; Serialize is not implemented for the secret.
Bounded by a configurable limit; exceeding it returns a typed error rather than an unbounded allocation.
WirekitError::InvalidConfig; no request is sent.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The HTTP status is authoritative and the reported detail is preserved.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: WirekitError::Api; the module does not fabricate a forecast.

edgeCases.description: Twilio signature verification over a form body with repeated or re-ordered parameters
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Canonical ordering is applied; a tampered parameter fails verification.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Verification fails; the raw body is never re-serialized.
WirekitError::Auth; no retry.
Throttled by the per-account bucket; remaining quota is visible in tracing.
The first code and message are surfaced and the full list is retained.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Verification fails (CON-215).

edgeCases.description: SendGrid attachment over the documented size limit
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Rejected before sending.

edgeCases.description: Slack HTTP 200 with ok: false and channel_not_found
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: WirekitError::Api; no retry.
Honored; channel data is cached to reduce repeated lookups.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Rejected as a replay.

risks.description: A single crate carrying 26+ provider features becomes a release and build-time bottleneck.
risks.mitigation: M1 ships four providers; measure build times and propose a companion crate if needed (CON-104 amendment path).

risks.description: 0.x churn in the error, retry, or auth contract breaks provider modules.
risks.mitigation: #[non_exhaustive], stable W#### codes, an additive-only feature policy, and shared-pipeline use until the 1.0 freeze.

risks.description: A dependency raises its MSRV above 1.85.
risks.mitigation: The MSRV CI job fails fast; pin or downgrade with a recorded decision.

risks.description: rustls versus native-tls surprises on a platform.
risks.mitigation: rustls is the default and a documented feature selects native-tls.

risks.description: A secret leaks into logs, traces, an error payload, a fixture, or an example.
risks.mitigation: Secret<T>, no Serialize for secret fields, redacted tracing fields, placeholder-only fixtures, and property tests from the Test agent.

risks.description: A provider needs behavior the pipeline cannot express.
risks.mitigation: The body-level error hook, per-provider retry and rate-limit overrides, injectable clients, and canonical-form signing hooks.

risks.description: The rate limiter blocks the async runtime or is unfair under concurrency.
risks.mitigation: Async token acquisition, per-provider buckets, and EC-015.

risks.description: Twilio A2P 10DLC or toll-free verification is a launch blocker for SMS at scale.
risks.mitigation: The module is sender-agnostic; registration is a consumer concern recorded as an open question, not a stub.

risks.description: SendGrid sender authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) or data residency limits real use.
risks.mitigation: The module is documented as transport-only; deliverability configuration stays with the consumer.

risks.description: Slack app review or scopes delay real use.
risks.mitigation: The module ships bot-token usage and documented scopes; the install flow is deferred to BP-015.

risks.description: NOAA polling across many workspaces is expensive in aggregate.
risks.mitigation: The optional grid/zone cache and a documented 15-minute polling budget.

risks.description: Provider error-shape drift (new codes, changed bodies) silently changes behavior.
risks.mitigation: Fixtures pin the shapes, unknown bodies map to WirekitError::Api rather than panicking, and tests are owned by /sdrive:test.

risks.description: Examples that need credentials cannot be verified in CI.
risks.mitigation: Examples compile in CI and exit with a clear message when credentials are absent; the NOAA example runs without a key.

risks.description: Scope creeps into other providers or stateful crates.
risks.mitigation: The explicit out-of-scope list; later work becomes a new version of this feature (CON-612).
